mutants.name: swapped_up_dn
mutants.description: Swapped UP/DN: the PFD drives pfd_up from the feedback flop and pfd_dn from the reference flop.

failure_messages.test_lock_deassert_dn:
cycle 24: expected a DN-only wide sample, got pfd_up=1 pfd_dn=0
assert (0 == 1)
failure_messages.test_pfd_dn_lead:
dt=5.0: pfd_dn width 0.0, expected 5.0
assert 5.0 <= 4.0
 +  where 5.0 = abs(-5.0)
failure_messages.test_pfd_frequency:
clk_fb slower: UP 0.0 ns should exceed DN 906.0 ns
assert 0.0 > 906.0
failure_messages.test_pfd_up_lead:
dt=5.0: pfd_up width 0.0, expected 5.0
assert 5.0 <= 4.0
 +  where 5.0 = abs(-5.0)
failure_messages.test_recover_pll_en:
change at 548219.717 ns is on no reference edge
assert 20.0 <= 4.0
 +  where 20.0 = abs((548239.717 - 548219.717))
failure_messages.test_recover_unlocked:
recovery lasted 10300.0 ns, expected 128 reference periods
assert 60.0 <= 1.0
 +  where 60.0 = abs((10300.0 - (128 * 80.0)))

mutants.name: missing_pfd_reset
mutants.description: Missing PFD reset: the delayed AND of up and dn (pfd_rst) no longer reaches the async clear, so pfd_clr is inactive whenever rst_n is high. The global rst_n term stays, so the flops still initialise and the fault is the missing PFD reset, not X propagation.

failure_messages.test_lock_assert:
10 ns UP pulse was judged wide
assert not True
 +  where True = any(<generator object test_lock_assert.<locals>.<genexpr> at 0x7302d101d700>)
failure_messages.test_lock_deassert:
lock not asserted before the wide cycle
assert 0 == 1
failure_messages.test_lock_deassert_dn:
cycle 24: expected a DN-only wide sample, got pfd_up=1 pfd_dn=1
assert (1 == 1 and 1 == 0)
failure_messages.test_pfd_dn_lead:
dt=5.0: pfd_dn pulsed 0 times
assert 0 >= 8
 +  where 0 = len([])
failure_messages.test_pfd_frequency:
clk_fb faster: DN 1600.0 ns should exceed UP 1600.0 ns
assert 1600.0 > 1600.0
failure_messages.test_pfd_up_lead:
dt=5.0: pfd_up pulsed 0 times
assert 0 >= 8
 +  where 0 = len([])
failure_messages.test_recover_lock_clears:
lock never rose and fell
assert ([])
 +  where [] = rises()
 +    where rises = <pll_ref.Monitor object at 0x7302d0db23c0>.rises
failure_messages.test_recover_pll_en:
expected one recovery, got []
assert 0 == 1
 +  where 0 = len([])
failure_messages.test_recover_unlocked:
expected two recoveries in 2334 cycles, got []
assert 0 == 2
 +  where 0 = len([])
